svg.title: Comparison of 3DGS-based pose refinement methods
svg.desc: Two dashed rounded base frames compare previous pose refinement and the proposed method. Left frame contains query image, pose estimator, bad pose prior, 3D Gaussian splatting, rendered image, rendered depth, and red bad-correspondence/bad-geometry annotations. Right frame contains the same core pipeline plus correspondence found, perturbation and importance sampling, Fisher information, uncertainty fields, geometric uncertainty heatmap, and a yellow where-to-focus region. Content is arranged left-to-right with vertical query-to-pose-to-prior chains and rendered outputs on the right of each pipeline.

g.desc: Origin is the left query image. Downward chain goes query image to pose estimator to bad pose prior; rightward chain goes to 3D Gaussian splatting and rendered outputs. Red annotations mark bad correspondence and bad geometry. Symmetry basis: two rendered outputs are vertically aligned at the right edge while the query-pose-prior stack is vertically centered on the left.

Origin is the right query image. The downward chain repeats query image, pose estimator, and bad pose prior, then moves right to perturbation and importance sampling feeding 3D Gaussian splatting. Rendered image/depth outputs align vertically, then arrows lead to uncertainty fields and geometric uncertainty. Symmetry basis: the right method extends the left pipeline horizontally into uncertainty estimation; rendered image and rendered depth remain vertically paired.
